subject: history_social
passage: Creole languages typically arise where people with no shared language are thrown together, as on colonial plantations: adults improvise a pidgin, a limited contact language, and children who grow up hearing it expand it into a full language with a complete grammar. Linguists have long noticed that creoles formed in widely separated places share certain grammatical habits, such as marking tense with separate small words placed before the verb. Some have taken these resemblances as evidence of an inborn human blueprint for grammar that children fall back on when the language around them is limited. Others counter that many of these creoles drew on related West African languages, whose shared features could simply have been passed along. Creoles whose speakers' languages had no such common source therefore carry special weight, since they can help separate the two explanations.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Creoles share grammatical features because children everywhere expand pidgins in the same inborn way.
choices.B: Most creole languages descend directly from West African languages rather than from pidgins.
choices.C: Linguists disagree about why creoles share features, and some creoles may help test the rival views.
choices.D: Pidgins become full languages only after adults add grammatical rules to them over several generations.

explanation.why: After explaining how creoles form, the text presents a puzzle (shared features across distant creoles) and two competing explanations: an inborn grammar or features inherited from related West African languages. It ends by identifying which creoles could help decide between them. The main idea must include both the disagreement and the way to test it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This presents one side of the debate as settled fact.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says creoles grow out of pidgins and that many drew on West African languages, not that they descend directly from them.
explanation.C: Correct. This captures both rival explanations and the text's point about which evidence could separate them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says children, not adults, expand pidgins into full languages.
